newsitem.title: UK: Britain not seeking confrontation with EU - Major.
newsitem.headline: Britain not seeking confrontation with EU - Major.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday he was not seeking confrontation with the European Union and he expected a worthwhile discussion when he met Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok this evening.

The Netherlands has just taken over the presidency of the EU for six months and Major told a news conference he would be discussing with Kok "what could be done both before and after the general election" -- referring to the forthcoming British general election, which has to be held by mid-May.
"I am not seeking confrontation with the European Union," Major said.
He said progress could be made in certain areas in the next few days, singling out "institutional change and the Commission" and "enshrining subsidiarity" in the EU's governing Treaty.
He did not specify what he described as "sticking points", but he said they were serious issues, not matters Britain was being difficult about for purely tactical reasons.
"I'm not expecting a row, I'm not expecting a fuss. I'm expecting...a worthwhile, detailed discussion of the serious issues," Major said.
Major was speaking at a the first in a series of news conference planned to boost his Conservative Party's standing in the run-up to the election.
